newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican crisis forced up to 20,000 companies shut.
newsitem.headline: Mexican crisis forced up to 20,000 companies shut.

text.p: Mexico's economic crisis after the peso's value plummeted starting in December 1994 forced up to 20,000 businesses to close, the president of Mexico's Business Coordinating Council said Wednesday.
"Between 1995 and 1996 we estimate 15,000 to 20,000 companies folded," Hector Larios told reporters.
The peso's value fell more than 60 percent in December 1994, putting thousands of people out of work.
Larios said emergency government measures helped prevent greater business collapses.
